module_title: The New Wage Definition & IR Code Thresholds
introduction: This intermediate tier drives into the heavily tested corporate compliance shifts. It details the revolutionary mathematical formula defining 'Wages', the massive relaxation of thresholds under the Industrial Relations Code, and the parity granted to Fixed-Term employees.

core_concepts.title: The New Definition of 'Wage' (The 50% Rule)
core_concepts.description:
A massive corporate compliance change to prevent companies from structuring pay to avoid PF/Gratuity contributions.
- The Rule: 'Wages' include Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance (DA) + Retaining Allowance. Allowances like HRA, conveyance, and overtime are *excluded*.
- The Catch (50% Limit): If these excluded allowances exceed **50 percent of the total remuneration**, the excess amount MUST be added back into the definition of 'Wages'. This ensures that at least 50% of an employee's salary is subject to Provident Fund and Gratuity deductions.

core_concepts.title: Industrial Relations (IR) Code: Relaxed Thresholds
core_concepts.description:
The IR Code dramatically alters the hiring and firing flexibility for companies (Ease of Doing Business).
- Standing Orders: The threshold for industrial establishments required to frame formal 'Standing Orders' (rules of conduct) has been increased from 100 workers to **300 workers**.
- Closure & Retrenchment: The threshold requiring prior government permission for lay-offs, retrenchment, and closure has also been increased from 100 to **300 workers**. Establishments with up to 299 workers can now fire staff or shut down without seeking state approval.

core_concepts.title: Fixed-Term Employment (FTE)
core_concepts.description:
The IR Code statutorily recognizes 'Fixed-Term Employment' as a distinct category, bypassing middlemen contractors.
- The Rule: An FTE is hired directly by the employer for a specific duration. They are legally entitled to the exact same hours of work, wages, and allowances as permanent workers. Furthermore, they are eligible for Gratuity on a pro-rata basis even if they work for less than 5 years (the usual requirement), provided they complete one year of service.

core_concepts.title: Universal Strike Notice
core_concepts.description:
Under the old Industrial Disputes Act, a mandatory 14-day notice before striking was only required for 'Public Utility Services' (like water, power, hospitals). 
- The New Rule: The IR Code 2020 makes a **14-day notice mandatory for ALL industrial establishments**. No worker can go on a legal strike without this notice.

important_entities.name: Reskilling Fund
important_entities.key_fact: A safety net for retrenched workers.
important_entities.significance: Under the IR Code, employers must contribute an amount equal to 15 days of the worker's last drawn wages to a 'Worker Reskilling Fund' when retrenching (firing) them. This fund helps the fired worker acquire new skills to rejoin the workforce.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced exams will test this distinction. A 'Contract Worker' is hired through a third-party middleman (Contractor) who takes a cut of the wages. A 'Fixed-Term Employee' is hired DIRECTLY by the principal employer on their payroll. The new Codes heavily incentivize Fixed-Term Employment to eliminate exploitative middlemen.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For any threshold question regarding Retrenchment, Closure, or Standing Orders under the new IR Code, the answer has been unilaterally increased to 300 workers.

exam_strategy_tips: If a CLAT PG question asks about the mathematical ceiling on excluded allowances in an employee's salary structure, immediately select **50 percent**.
